evals.prompt: Дедушка ушёл на фронт в 1941 году и пропал без вести. Знаем только, что звали его Абрам Гершкович, фамилия Гольдберг, родился примерно в 1910 году где-то под Винницей. Найди его в Памяти народа и ОБД.
evals.expected_output: First builds an identification set (surname variants Гольдберг/Гольдберк/Гольдбер, given name Абрам/Аркадий, patronymic Гершкович/Григорьевич/Гиршевич, years 1908–1912, place of birth — establish the district). Searches OBD with each spelling as a separate query (the search is exact); in Pamyat Naroda uses the place-of-birth filter and reviews the fuzzy matches; explains that a human passes the captcha; adds martyrology.org.ua (Vinnytsia oblast, search by the start of the surname). Checks candidates by year and place of birth, opens the scans of loss reports and hospital registers (relatives' address). Records findings with the record's address, a verbatim quotation of the fields and a check against the scan; a negative result comes with the list of spellings and databases.

evals.prompt: Семья бабушки эвакуировалась в Ташкент из Киева в 1941-м. Бабушке было лет пять. Как найти их эвакокарточки и что в них может быть полезного?
evals.expected_output: Names the Tashkent database on JewishGen (about 152,000 cards, fields with the patronymic, scan by number, limit — arrivals before February 1942) and the evacuation lists at Yad Vashem (and USHMM, with a warning that the database has moved to a new site and the old address closes in autumn 2026). Advises reading the cards in full: patronymic, occupation, place of work, family composition, address of accommodation; comparing the paths to the scan images — a match means one page of a list, that is one family. Warns that a child may be written into a parent's card rather than have one of their own, that names may be in a Soviet form, and that absence from the Tashkent database does not prove the family was not there. Proposes searching both by the place of departure and by the place of accommodation.

evals.prompt: Прадед был арестован в 1937 году в Житомире, больше о нём ничего не слышали. В семье его звали Мойше, а по документам вроде Михаил Борисович. Где искать?
evals.expected_output: Explains Soviet name changes (Мойше → Михаил; the patronymic Борисович may stand for Беркович or Борухович) and goes through the forms. Points to Open List (prefix search over all spellings, search by place without a surname, a pause of at least 6 s), Immortal Barracks (Bessmertny barak), and Ukrainian sources: the Archive of National Memory (HDA UINP), the sectoral archive of the SBU, the National data bank of the repressed, the oblast archive. Notes that personal files are closed for 75 years and are issued to relatives, and that letters and requests are made only by the person. Requires recording the file reference and a verbatim quotation; treats a match by the name table as a hypothesis until checked by a second identifier.
